newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty eases vs basket, depos stable.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty eases vs basket, depos stable.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased against the basket of currencies in slow trade after an early bout of position closing created a light currency buying mood which took the Polish unit off Wednesday highs, dealers said.
They said the afternoon zloty drifted mostly sideways reflecting a steady European dollar/mark, hovering between 2.8070-80 against the dollar and 1.8640-50 against the mark.
"After the morning swing the zloty was locked in a narrow range mirroring today's steady dollar/mark in European trade," said Lukasz Kowalski from Deutsche Bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 2.15/2.13 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Wednesday's 2.29/2.26 percent from parity.
It closed at 2.8076/82 to the dollar, down from 2.8038/50 on Wednesday and at 1.8640/48 to the mark, down from 1.8620/25.
Dealers said large zloty swings were unlikely without the support of foreign orders tomorrow and predicted the range for zloty trade at between 2.0 and 2.2 percent from parity.

Interbank deposits rates barely changed on the balanced market. Overnight deposits rates were at 19.05/19.25 percent against opening's 19.05/19.15 percent. Tomorrow/next rates were flat at 19.10/19.30 percent.

The central bank refrained from draining the market for the second day in a row. Analysts said the NBP was likely to limit its drainages in November to allow reserve money to grow to levels it had set.

"The central bank is not likely to want higher market rates in the near future, because drainages could pull down reserve money growth below the lower band of the November target," said Marek Zelinski from Bank Slaski SA.
The NBP set the November band at 33.29 and 33.99 billion zlotys, which means reserve money must grow at least 293 million zlotys in November to finnish within the targeted band.

The average level of reserve money in October rose only 198 million zlotys to 33 billion zlotys and was only 47 million zlotys above the lower edge of the central banks' band at between 32.95 and 33.65 billion zlotys.
